title: 1963 AHSME Problem 16
statement: Three numbers \(a,\) \(b,\) \(c,\) none zero, form an arithmetic progression. Increasing \(a\) by \(1\) or increasing \(c\) by \(2\) results in a geometric progression. Then \(b\) equals:

solutions.text:
The conditions give \[ \begin{gathered} 2b=a+c,\\ b^2=(a+1)c,\qquad b^2=a(c+2). \end{gathered} \] Comparing the last two yields \(c=2a.\) Thus \(b=\frac{3a}{2},\) and \(\frac{9a^2}{4}=2a(a+1).\) Since \(a\ne0,\) \(a=8,\) so \(b=12.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is C.
